implementation_notes: The default realization: one enum whose variants carry the parameters, `#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]` emitting the discriminator that the far side dispatches on with an exhaustive `match`, and serde_json/bincode/postcard providing the codec. The compiler proves every command is handled, there is no registry and no reflection, and the wire contract is the variant names plus field names - which must therefore be pinned with serde renames. It is closed by construction: a command set extended from other crates needs the typetag variant instead.
pitfalls: Internally tagged enums cannot hold tuple variants (a serde limitation), and the tag is the variant name: renaming a variant breaks every queued message unless #[serde(rename = ...)] pins the wire name.

Non-self-describing formats (bincode, postcard) encode enums by variant INDEX unless told otherwise, so reordering variants silently reinterprets old messages - pin explicit tags or a discriminator field for durable queues.
Deserialising into serde_json::Value and unwrapping later skips the type check at the boundary: decode into the enum before dispatch and route unknown variants to a dead-letter path.

variants.name: typetag-registered trait objects for an open command set
variants.implementation_notes: When commands must be pluggable across crates, the closed enum cannot be used: `#[typetag::serde] trait Command` registers each implementor at link time, and serde deserialises `Box<dyn Command>` by reading the type tag and looking the concrete implementation up in that registry - the closest Rust analogue of the classic polymorphic command base. The price is a global registry, no compile-time exhaustiveness, and a runtime error when a tag is not linked in; prefer the enum variant unless open extension is a real requirement.
pitfalls: Registration happens at link time: whether a tag resolves depends on which crates are linked into the worker, so a missing command is a runtime deserialisation error - surface it into a dead-letter path rather than restarting.
The default type tag is the Rust type name, so crate/type renames break old messages unless explicit stable tags are given.
Trait objects reintroduce dynamic dispatch and prohibit generic methods on the trait; if the command set is really closed, the enum variant is faster and safer.
